pre_mortem: If this correction closure is wrong, the most likely path is a future performance change adding memoization to load_native_codex_schema() without re-auditing native_codex_provider_response_schema(), on the assumption the deepcopy already reviewed here still applies after refactoring -- if a later edit removes or bypasses the deepcopy call while keeping the same function name and docstring, historical plan_result validation could silently start requiring finding_dispositions again, exactly reproducing the C-03 failure mode this round closed.

review_evidence.break_condition: This disposition breaks if a full-matrix run shows native_codex_provider_response_schema() still mutates a shared/aliased object reachable from load_native_codex_schema() (e.g. via later caching), if the historical-read-before-provider-schema test ordering is not exactly as shown in the diff, or if any remaining code path still references a require_structured parameter on replay_findings().
review_evidence.dimensions: Scope-limited verification of the two BLOCKER/OBSERVATION items owned by this round: (1) schema-object aliasing safety -- confirmed native_codex_provider_response_schema() constructs its mutable copy via copy.deepcopy(load_native_codex_schema()) before appending to the copy's required list, and never touches the object load_native_codex_schema() itself returns; (2) test ordering fidelity -- test_historical_plan_result_without_dispositions_remains_readable in tests/test_native_codex_contract.py invokes the provider-schema builder before the persisted-schema loader and the historical parse, matching the C-03 acceptance test's required call order and thereby actually exercising the aliasing failure mode rather than accidentally avoiding it; (3) parameter cleanup -- grep-equivalent inspection of the supplied diff shows replay_findings()'s signature, docstring, and its one production caller (orchestrator.py authoritative_native_findings) are all consistent with require_structured having been fully removed, with no stale references left in the reviewed hunks; (4) non-regression of C-01/C-02 -- the correction diff touches only the schema-copy mechanics and the replay_findings signature/docstring, neither of which alters the mirror-vs-replay guard behavior or the plan_result backward-compatibility contract those findings closed on.
review_evidence.largest_residual_risk: This review trusted the supplied fingerprint-bound attestation (1156 passed in 188.82s) rather than independently executing tests, per the review instruction; if that attestation does not actually correspond to the diff content shown (e.g. a mismatched fingerprint or an unattested local edit), the closures here would rest on unverified claims about test_historical_plan_result_without_dispositions_remains_readable actually passing with the shown call order.

status_changes.rationale: native_codex_provider_response_schema() now does `schema = copy.deepcopy(load_native_codex_schema())` before appending 'finding_dispositions' to schema["$defs"]["plan_result"]["required"], so the mutation can no longer alias into whatever load_native_codex_schema() returns even if that loader becomes cached/shared later. The new regression test test_historical_plan_result_without_dispositions_remains_readable calls native_codex_provider_response_schema() FIRST, then load_native_codex_schema() SECOND, then parses a historical plan_result document -- exactly the ordering the bound acceptance test demanded to catch an aliasing leak -- and asserts 'finding_dispositions' is present in the provider schema's required list but absent from the persisted schema's required list, with the historical document still parsing to findings==(). This satisfies the acceptance test: build the live provider schema first, then prove the persisted schema still omits finding_dispositions from required and a historical plan result still parses, using a defensive copy before live mutation.

The `require_structured` parameter has been removed from replay_findings(); its signature is now `replay_findings(replay, work_unit_id=None)`. The function's docstring explicitly documents that historical/unstructured finding-transition records remain valid general replay inputs but are unconditionally excluded from finding-authority projection because they lack a persisted work_unit_id and therefore cannot safely authorize a new native request under possible cross-work-unit identifier reuse. orchestrator.py's ProductionWorkflowDriver.authoritative_native_findings (the sole caller) now invokes replay_findings(replay) without the removed flag, so there is no dangling reference to the eliminated parameter. This satisfies the acceptance test's first option: remove the unused parameter and document unconditional exclusion of legacy transitions.
